D18a's rule bites: fps decline is a *receiver* observation, the ladder is a *sender* control, and there is no back-channel — so \"step the ladder down\" is **structurally impossible** here. Mitigate locally instead: **duty-cycle (D27)** is the primary lever; drop decode resolution is often NOT viable because S3 showed 1080p was already at 2.25 camera px/module (below the 4 px/module cliff), and 720p measured 100% erasure. Resolution reduction MUST maintain ≥ 4 camera px/module floor. **Detection:** Decode latency increases >50% while camera fps stays within -20%. See `docs/notes/bf-3mnt-thermal-throttling-discrimination.md` for discrimination logic against sender-side throttling. |\n990\t| E18 | **Resume offered for a file the user no longer has** (sender side) | `streamId` mismatch on re-selection → offer a fresh transfer, do not silently restart. |\n991\t\n992\t---\n993\t\n994\t## 11. Error taxonomy\n995\t\n996\tEvery distinguishable condition gets a stable code and one user-facing sentence. Defined\n997\tnow, before Phase 5 designs any UI — after that, taxonomies get retrofitted to screens.\n998\t\n999\t**Optical / acquisition** (the stall detector's job, `bf-5vm`):\n1000\t\n1001\t| Code | Meaning | User-facing |\n1002\t|---|---|---|\n1003\t| `E-NO-SIGNAL` | No decodable tiles at all | \"Point the camera at the sending screen.\" |\n1004\t| `E-TOO-FAR` | **camera** px/module < 4 (§2) | \"Move closer — the code is too small to read.\" |\n1005\t| `E-TOO-CLOSE` | Symbol exceeds frame, or below min focus | \"Move back a little.\" |\n1006\t| `E-BLUR` | Sharpness metric below threshold | \"Hold steady.\" |\n1007\t| `E-DARK` | Insufficient exposure | \"Too dark — raise the sender's screen brightness.\" |\n1008\t| `E-GLARE` | Saturated region over the code | \"Tilt to avoid the reflection.\" |\n1009\t| `E-FOCUS-HUNT` | Focus oscillating | \"Tap the screen to lock focus.\" |\n1010\t| `E-ORIENTATION` | Detected capture aspect doesn't match the sender's configured setting (§6.3.2) — e.g. sender is shaping the code for landscape but the receiver is held portrait | \"This app works fine held normally — but if you'd like more margin, match the orientation setting on the sending device, or turn the phone sideways.\" (tip, not a blocker — portrait is fully supported) |\n1011\t| `E-SENDER-STALLED` | Identical frames repeating | \"The sending device seems paused.\" |\n1012\t| `E-TORN` | Torn-frame rate high | \"Lower the sender's frame rate.\" |\n1013\t\n1014\t**Protocol:**\n1015\t\n1016\t| Code | Meaning | User-facing | Recovery |\n1017\t|---|---|---|---|\n1018\t| `E-FOREIGN-STREAM` | Different `streamId` (E7) | \"That's a different file — ignoring it.\" | automatic, informational |\n1019\t| `E-VERSION` | Unknown `magic_ver` (§16.3) | \"The sending device is running version X; this one is Y. Update both.\" | user must update |\n1020\t| `E-META-BOUNDS` | Beacon field out of bounds (T1) | \"That transmission looks malformed and was rejected.\" | automatic, refuse |\n1021\t| `E-MANIFEST-CORRUPT` | Manifest CRC validation failed (§7.6) | \"The block manifest is corrupted and is being re-decoded.\" | automatic retry |\n1022\t| `E-MANIFEST-MISSING` | Manifest never arrived (§7.6) | \"Waiting for block manifest to verify received chunks.\" | wait or request repair |\n1023\t| `E-MANIFEST-DECODE` | Manifest fountain decode failed (§7.6) | \"Could not decode the block manifest. Retrying...\" | automatic retry |\n1024\t| `E-MANIFEST-LIVELOCK` | E12 livelock detected, manifest corrupted (bf-5fm) | \"Multiple chunks failed verification — the manifest appears corrupted. Re-decoding manifest...\" | re-decode manifest |\n1025\t| `E-BLOCK-HASH` | Rank K reached, hash failed (E12) | \"A chunk arrived corrupted and is being re-collected.\" | automatic retry |\n1026\t| `E-BLOCK-RETRY-EXCEEDED` | Block retry limit exceeded (E12 livelock, bf-5fm) | \"A chunk has failed verification too many times. Re-decoding manifest...\" | re-decode manifest |\n1027\t| `E-K-OVERFLOW` | Sender K exceeds receiver's maximum (D26) | \"Sender's chunk size is too large for this device. Use a smaller file or a more powerful receiver.\" | refuse, user adjusts |\n1028\t| `E-REPAIR-BOUNDS` | Repair code references blocks beyond file (§8.2) | \"That repair code refers to chunks that don't exist. Check it and try again.\" | user re-enters |\n1029\t| `E-REPAIR-CODE` | Repair code checksum failed | \"That repair code doesn't look right — check it and try again.\" | user re-enters |\n1030\t| `E-FILE-HASH` | Whole-file hash failed (E13) | \"The file is complete but failed its final check — saved as unverified.\" | keep output, warn |\n1031\t| `E-WASM-LOAD` | Decoder failed to load | \"The scanner failed to start. Reload the page.\" | user reloads |\n1032\t\n1033\t**Status codes** (informational, not errors):\n1034\t\n1035\t| Code | Meaning | User-facing |\n1036\t|---|---|---|\n1037\t| `E-VERIFYING` | Verifying blocks against manifest (§7.6) | \"Verifying received chunks against manifest...\" |\n1038\t\n1039\t**Local / resource:**\n1040\t\n1041\t| Code | Meaning | User-facing | Recovery |\n1042\t|---|---|---|---|\n1043\t| `E-QUOTA-PREFLIGHT` | Not enough storage (§13.1) | \"Not enough free space: this needs X, you have Y.\" | user frees space |\n1044\t| `E-QUOTA-EXHAUSTED` | Ran out mid-transfer (E10) | \"Out of space. Saved what arrived — X of Y chunks.\" | partial export |\n1045\t| `E-SOURCE-CHANGED` | Source mutated (E5) | \"The file changed while sending. Start again to avoid a corrupt copy.\" | restart required |\n1046\t| `E-BACKGROUNDED` | Sender tab backgrounded (E8) | \"Sending paused — keep this tab visible.\" | auto-resume on focus |\n1047\t| `E-CAMERA-LOST` | Permission revoked (E9) | \"Camera access ended. Your progress is saved.\" | re-grant, resume |\n1048\t| `E-WAKELOCK-LOST` | Screen may sleep | \"The screen may turn off. Adjust your sleep settings.\" | user acts |\n1049\t| `E-DECOMPRESS` | Decompression failed (E15) | \"Everything arrived but couldn't be unpacked. The raw data was kept.\" | keep artefact |\n1050\t\n1051\t---\n1052\t\n1053\t## 12. Threat model\n1054\t\n1055\tThe README claims \"provably no exfiltration\" and \"auditable once and trusted thereafter\".\n1056\tThat claim needs backing. In scope for v1:\n1057\t\n1058\t| # | Threat | Stance | Test |\n1059\t|---|---|---|---|\n1060\t| **T1** | **Crafted optical stream — resource exhaustion.** Beacon-declared `originalSize` and `payloadLen` (281 TB each), `blockCount` (16.7 M) and `L` are attacker-controlled and size allocations. | **Mitigated.** Bounds-check every beacon field before use: `L` ∈ [1, 4096], `K` ≤ locally benchmarked max (D26), `blockCount` ≤ 16.7 M, `originalSize` ≤ available quota, `payloadLen` ≤ available quota. Reject with `E-META-BOUNDS`. Never allocate from a declared size. | A10 + fuzz beacon fields |\n1061\t| **T2** | **Path traversal / hostile filename.** `filename` is attacker-supplied and reaches a save dialog. | **Mitigated.** Strip path separators, control bytes and leading dots; cap length; never pass through unsanitised. | unit: filenames with `../`, NUL, control bytes |\n1062\t| **T3** | **Decompression bomb.** The receiver decompresses attacker-supplied data. | **Mitigated.** Enforce a max expansion ratio (100:1) and an absolute cap = declared `originalSize`; abort with `E-DECOMPRESS` on overrun. | unit: 1 GB-expanding zip bomb → `E-DECOMPRESS` |\n1063\t| **T4a** | **Sender-side plaintext residue.** D8 writes a *decompressed-equivalent* copy of the user's file to OPFS as staging. For the flagship use case (SSH keys, PSBTs, TOTP seeds) this is real exposure. | **Mitigated.** Wipe staging on completion, on cancel, and on startup-reap (E11). Document that OPFS is not encrypted at rest and the OS/browser may retain it. | integration: assert sender OPFS empty after complete/cancel/reap |\n1064\t| **T4b** | **Receiver-side plaintext residue.** The receiver stages the complete decoded file in OPFS. The receiver derives K from the beacon and MUST refuse a stream whose K exceeds what it benchmarked locally.\"\n18\t\n19\tWithout this component:\n20\t- A sender could transmit K=768 to a low-end device that can only sustain K=512\n21\t- The receiver's GE decoder would fall behind, causing frame drops and transfer failure\n22\t- This creates a resource exhaustion attack vector (T1)\n23\t\n24\t## Component Design\n25\t\n26\t### 1. Benchmark Algorithm\n27\t\n28\tPort the existing `spike/ge-bench.mjs` algorithm to run in browser context:\n29\t\n30\t```typescript\n31\t// src/platform/ge-benchmark.ts\n32\texport interface GEBenchmarkResult {\n33\t  deviceSignature: string;       // UA + platform fingerprint\n34\t  measuredThroughputMBs: number;  // MB/s sustained XOR\n35\t  derivedKMax: number;           // Max K this device can handle\n36\t  timestamp: number;             // When benchmark was run\n37\t}\n38\t\n39\texport interface GEBenchmarkConfig {\n40\t  stages: Array<{name: string, rateKBs: number}>;  // Wire rates to test\n41\t  phoneFactor: number;                               // Safety margin (÷4 default)\n42\t  targetK: number;                                   // K to test (768 default)\n43\t}\n44\t```\n45\t\n46\t**Benchmark procedure:**\n47\t1. Run complete GF(2) GE decode for K=768, L=256\n48\t2. Measure sustained XOR throughput (MB/s)\n49\t3. Apply safety margin (÷4 for desktop→phone estimate)\n50\t4. Derive K_max from the required throughput formula\n51\t\n52\t**Required throughput formula (from §3.1):**\n53\t```\n54\trequired(K, L, wireRate) = K · (K/8 + L) · wireRate / L\n55\t```\n56\t\n57\t**Derive K_max:**\n58\t- Binary search or table lookup to find max K where:\n59\t  `measured_throughput ≥ required(K, 256, stage3_rate)`\n60\t\n61\t### 2. Caching Strategy\n62\t\n63\tCache results in IndexedDB with a composite key:\n64\t\n65\t```typescript\n66\tinterface CacheKey {\n67\t  userAgent: string;          // Navigator UA\n68\t  platform: string;           // 'Win32', 'Linux x86_64', etc.\n69\t  hardwareConcurrency: number; // CPU core count\n70\t  deviceMemory: number;       // GB if available\n71\t}\n72\t\n73\tinterface CachedResult {\n74\t  key: CacheKey;\n75\t  result: GEBenchmarkResult;\n76\t  version: number;            // Benchmark algo version (for invalidation)\n77\t}\n78\t```\n79\t\n80\t**Cache invalidation:**\n81\t- Version bump when benchmark algorithm changes\n82\t- Optional: time-based expiry (30 days)\n83\t- Manual: user-triggered \"re-benchmark\" in health check UI\n84\t\n85\t### 3. Integration with Health Check (§16.4)\n86\t\n87\tThe health check runs before the user commits to receiving a file. Current checklist (§16.4):\n88\t- Storage estimate (bf-4d6)\n89\t- Camera capability and measured fps (D14)\n90\t- Wake lock availability\n91\t- OPFS write test\n92\t- Calibration probe (D11)\n93\t\n94\t**Add:** GE benchmark (this component)\n95\t\n96\t```typescript\n97\t// src/platform/health-check.ts\n98\texport interface HealthCheckResult {\n99\t  storage: {available: boolean, quota?: number};\n100\t  camera: {available: boolean, measuredFps?: number};\n101\t  wakeLock: {available: boolean};\n102\t  opfs: {available: boolean, writeTestPassed?: boolean};\n103\t  geBenchmark: {available: boolean, kMax?: number};  // NEW\n104\t  calibration: {lumaWins: boolean | null};  // D11\n105\t}\n106\t\n107\texport async function runHealthCheck(): Promise<HealthCheckResult> {\n108\t  return {\n109\t    storage: await checkStorage(),\n110\t    camera: await checkCamera(),\n111\t    wakeLock: await checkWakeLock(),\n112\t    opfs: await checkOPFS(),\n113\t    geBenchmark: await runGEBenchmark(),  // NEW\n114\t    calibration: await runCalibrationProbe(),\n115\t  };\n116\t}\n117\t```\n118\t\n119\t### 4. Stream Validation (D26/T1 Enforcement)\n120\t\n121\tOn beacon receipt, before allocating any GE structures:\n122\t\n123\t```typescript\n124\t// src/core/frame/beacon.ts (or validation layer)\n125\texport function validateBeacon(meta: BeaconMeta, localKMax: number): void {\n126\t  // ... existing bounds checks (fileSize, blockCount, L, etc.)\n127\t  \n128\t  // NEW: D26 K validation\n129\t  const derivedK = Math.ceil(meta.blockSize / L);\n130\t  if (derivedK > localKMax) {\n131\t    throw new StreamRefusedError(\n132\t      'E-K-OVERFLOW',\n133\t      `Sender K (${derivedK}) exceeds this device's maximum (${localKMax}). ` +\n134\t      `Reduce file size or use a more powerful receiver.`,\n135\t      {derivedK, localKMax}\n136\t    );\n137\t  }\n138\t}\n139\t```\n140\t\n141\t### 5. Error Code\n142\t\n143\t**Error code:** `E-K-OVERFLOW` (new addition to §11 error taxonomy)\n144\t\n145\t| Field | Value |\n146\t|-------|-------|\n147\t| Code | `E-K-OVERFLOW` |\n148\t| Category | Protocol |\n149\t| Meaning | Beacon-derived K exceeds local device's benchmarked K_max |\n150\t| User-facing | \"That transmission is too complex for this device. Use a smaller file or a more powerful receiver.\" |\n151\t| Recovery | User must act on the OTHER device (reduce file size → smaller K), or use a desktop as receiver |\n152\t\n153\t**Why not `E-META-BOUNDS`**: T1 groups this under meta bounds, but K_overflow is a distinct condition with different recovery (it's about computational capacity, not malformed data). Keeping it separate makes debugging and telemetry clearer.\n154\t\n155\t### 6. Worker Architecture\n156\t\n157\tRun the benchmark in a dedicated worker to avoid janking the UI:\n158\t\n159\t```typescript\n160\t// src/workers/ge-benchmark.worker.ts\n161\texport interface BenchmarkMessage {\n162\t  type: 'run';\n163\t  config: GEBenchmarkConfig;\n164\t}\n165\t\n166\texport interface BenchmarkResultMessage {\n167\t  type: 'result';\n168\t  result: GEBenchmarkResult;\n169\t}\n170\t\n171\t// Worker spins up, runs the GE decode loop (ported from spike/ge-bench.mjs),\n172\t// measures throughput, posts back result, self-terminates.\n173\t```\n174\t\n175\t**Main thread:**\n176\t1. Spawn worker\n177\t2. Send config\n178\t3. Await result\n179\t4. Cache to IndexedDB\n180\t5. Return to caller\n181\t\n182\t### 7. Fallback and Graceful Degradation\n183\t\n184\tIf the benchmark fails to run (e.g., worker crash, timeout):\n185\t\n186\t```typescript\n187\texport const FALLBACK_K_MAX = 512;  // Conservative default\n188\t\n189\texport async function getKMaxWithFallback(): Promise<number> {\n190\t  try {\n191\t    const cached = await loadCachedBenchmark();\n192\t    if (cached) return cached.derivedKMax;\n193\t    \n194\t    const fresh = await runGEBenchmark();\n195\t    await cacheBenchmark(fresh);\n196\t    return fresh.derivedKMax;\n197\t  } catch (e) {\n198\t    console.warn('GE benchmark failed, using fallback K_max=512', e);\n199\t    return FALLBACK_K_MAX;\n200\t  }\n201\t}\n202\t```\n203\t\n204\t**Rationale for K=512 fallback:**\n205\t- Stage 3 required: 69.5 MB/s at K=512 (from §3.1 table)\n206\t- After ÷4 phone factor: desktop needs 278 MB/s\n207\t- S1 measured 3,260 MB/s on desktop → 11.7× margin\n208\t- Even if phone is 8× slower (not 4×), 512 works\n209\t\n210\t### 8. Glossary\n75\t\n76\tSeveral of these words are overloaded in the surrounding literature, and two of them\n77\t(*block*, *frame*) mean different things in different research documents. Within this\n78\tplan they mean exactly this:\n79\t\n80\t| Term | Meaning here |\n81\t|---|---|\n82\t| **Fragment** | The atomic unit the fountain code operates over. Duty-cycling must be **block-granular**, not frame-granular: the receiver knows blockIndex from the header (§7.1), so it decodes block N at full attention and skips N+1 entirely. This doubles the number of passes but completes transfers where frame-granular duty cycling would never finish (frame-granular 50% duty on 25% erasure delivers only 0.60 K against the 1.03 K needed at dwell 1.6). No web API exposes SoC temperature, so sustained fps decline is the proxy (E17b). **Throttling discrimination:** Before applying duty-cycling, the receiver MUST distinguish sender-side throttling (E17a) from receiver-side throttling (E17b) using the multi-metric approach specified in `docs/notes/bf-3mnt-thermal-throttling-discrimination.md`. Sender-side throttling is detected when camera fps drops >30% while decode latency stays within +30%; in this case, the receiver MUST NOT duty-cycle. Receiver-side throttling is detected when decode latency increases >50% while camera fps stays within -20%; in this case, D27's block-granular duty-cycling applies. | `spike-results`, R11, `bf-3mnt` |\n250\t| **D25** | **Cap fountain degree at d ≤ 64** | Cuts encoder XOR **7.9×** at the adopted K = 768 (mean degree 106.3 → 13.5): 12.2 MB/s → 1.6 MB/s at 450 packets/s (R2 nominal: 2 packets/tile, 15 tiles, 15 fps). K, K);\n    const cum = new Float64Array(hi);\n    let total = 0;\n    for (let d = 1; d <= hi; d++) total += 1 / d;\n    let acc = 0;\n    for (let d = 1; d <= hi; d++) {\n      acc += 1 / d / total;\n      cum[d - 1] = acc;\n    }\n    return () => {\n      const r = rnd();\n      let lo = 0,\n        high = hi - 1;\n      while (lo < high) {\n        const mid = (lo + high) >> 1;\n        if (cum[mid] < r) lo = mid + 1;\n        else high = mid;\n      }\n      return lo + 1;\n    };\n  }\n\n  // Run the benchmark\n  let bestThroughput = 0;\n  let bestPackets = 0;\n  let bestRowOps = 0;\n  let bestMs = 0;\n\n  // Warm up and take best of 3 trials\n  for (let trial = -1; // 32 bytes\n  manifestHash: Uint8Array; // 4 bytes - CRC-32 of manifest (roots beacon->manifest->blocks chain)\n  filename: string;\n  mimeType: string;\n}\n\n/**\n * Validation error with code and details.\n */\nexport class BeaconValidationError extends Error {\n  constructor(\n    public code: string,\n    message: string,\n    public details: Record<string, unknown>\n  ) {\n    super(message);\n    this.name = 'BeaconValidationError';\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Maximum safe values for beacon fields (T1).\n *\n * **Beacon size bound calculation (R1's 256-byte payload):**\n * - Fixed fields: 64 bytes (streamId, wireVersion, originalSize, payloadLen, blockSize,\n *                  blockCount, fragmentLen, degreeCap, flags, blockHashLen,\n *                  wholeFileHash, manifestHash)\n * - CRC-32: 4 bytes\n * - Length prefixes: 2 bytes (1 byte each for filename and mimeType)\n * - Available for filename + mimeType: 256 - 64 - 4 - 2 = 186 bytes\n *\n * This yields a conservative allocation of 128 bytes for filename and 58 bytes for\n * mimeType, ensuring the beacon never overflows R1's capacity while accommodating\n * common filenames and MIME types.\n */\nexport const BEACON_LIMITS = {\n  MAX_L: 4096,\n  MAX_BLOCK_COUNT: 16_700_000, // 16.7M blocks × 192 KB = 3.0 TB\n  MAX_FILE_SIZE: 281_474_976_710_656, // 281 TB, 6-byte field max\n  /** Maximum number of blocks that the manifest itself can consume (T1). */\n  /** K_manifest = ceil(blockCount × blockHashLen / BLOCK). Limits DoS from unbounded manifest growth. */\n  MAX_K_MANIFEST_BLOCKS: 1000, // 1000 manifest blocks ≈ 195 MB of manifest data\n  /** Maximum UTF-8 encoded filename length in bytes (T2). Chosen to fit within R1's 256-byte payload. */\n  MAX_FILENAME_BYTES: 128,\n  /** Maximum UTF-8 encoded MIME type length in bytes (T2). Chosen to fit within R1's 256-byte payload. */\n  MAX_MIMETYPE_BYTES: 58,\n  /** Maximum UTF-8 codepoint count for filename (T2). A UTF-8 string can use up to 4 bytes per codepoint. */\n  MAX_FILENAME_CODEPOINTS: 32, // 32 × 4 = 128, guarantees never exceeds MAX_FILENAME_BYTES\n  /** Maximum UTF-8 codepoint count for MIME type (T2). */\n  MAX_MIMETYPE_CODEPOINTS: 14, // 14 × 4 = 56, fits within MAX_MIMETYPE_BYTES\n} as const;\n\n/**\n * Calculate K_manifest from blockCount and blockHashLen.\n *\n * K_manifest is the number of blocks needed to store the block hash manifest.\n * The manifest contains blockCount × blockHashLen bytes (all block hashes),\n * divided into blocks of size BLOCK (196608 bytes = K × L).\n *\n * Formula: K_manifest = ceil(blockCount × blockHashLen / BLOCK)\n *\n * @param blockCount - Number of data blocks (from beacon)\n * @param blockHashLen - Length of each block hash in bytes (from beacon)\n * @returns Number of blocks needed to store the manifest\n */\nfunction calculateKManifest(blockCount: number, blockHashLen: number): number {\n  const BLOCK = 196608; // K × L where K=768, L=256 (from core/params.ts)\n  const manifestBytes = blockCount * blockHashLen;\n  return Math.ceil(manifestBytes / BLOCK);\n}\n\n/**\n * Device context for K validation logging.\n */\nexport interface DeviceContext {\n  /** Device signature from GE benchmark cache */\n  deviceSignature: string;\n  /** User agent string */\n  userAgent: string;\n  /** Platform identifier */\n  platform: string;\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse a beacon from bytes.\n *\n * Beacon format: [body fields...][crc32(4)]\n * The CRC-32 covers all beacon body fields and MUST be validated before\n * any metadata (including streamId) is trusted.\n *\n * **Validation order is critical:**\n * 1. @throws {BeaconValidationError} If any field fails validation or CRC-32 mismatch\n */\nexport function parseBeacon(\n  bytes: Uint8Array,\n  localKMax: number,\n  availableQuota: number,\n  deviceContext?: DeviceContext\n): BeaconMeta {\n  let offset = 0;\n\n  const readU32 = (): number => {\n    const value = (bytes[offset]! << 24) |\n                 (bytes[offset + 1]! << 16) |\n                 (bytes[offset + 2]! << 8) |\n                 bytes[offset + 3]!;\n    offset += 4;\n    return value >>> 0; // Force unsigned\n  };\n\n  const readU24 = (): number => {\n    const value = (bytes[offset]! << 16) |\n                 (bytes[offset + 1]! << 8) |\n                 bytes[offset + 2]!;\n    offset += 3;\n    return value >>> 0;\n  };\n\n  const readU16 = (): number => {\n    const value = (bytes[offset]! << 8) | bytes[offset + 1]!;\n    offset += 2;\n    return value >>> 0;\n  };\n\n  const readU8 = (): number => {\n    const value = bytes[offset]!;\n    offset += 1;\n    return value;\n  };\n\n  const readBytes = (n: number): Uint8Array => {\n    const value = bytes.subarray(offset, offset + n);\n    offset += n;\n    return value;\n  };\n\n  const readString = expected ${expectedSize} (body+CRC)`,\n      {actual: bytes.length, expected: expectedSize}\n    );\n  }\n\n  // Read the CRC-32 from the last 4 bytes\n  const storedCrc = ((bytes[offset]! << 24) |\n beacon body (everything except the last 4 bytes)\n  const calculatedCrc = crc32(bytes.subarray(0, beaconBodySize));\n\n  if (storedCrc !== calculatedCrc) {\n    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n      'E-CRC-MISMATCH',\n      `Beacon CRC-32 mismatch: stored=${storedCrc} calculated=${calculatedCrc}`,\n      {stored: storedCrc, calculated: calculatedCrc}\n    );\n  }\n\n  // blockHashLen);\n  if (blockCountManifest > BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_K_MANIFEST_BLOCKS) {\n    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n      'E-META-BOUNDS',\n      `Manifest block count (${blockCountManifest})
